facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old man presented with gross hematuria
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: Intravenous urography and retrograde ureteropyelography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter, consistent with a ureteral polyp.

aliases: Transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter
concepts.why: Although urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy, the presence of a ureteral mass and partial obstruction raises the possibility of ureteral carcinoma.
The tubular filling defect and partial obstruction of the right mid ureter could also be consistent with a ureteral stricture.
The patient's presentation with gross hematuria and intermittent right pelvic pain, along with the finding of microscopic hematuria, raises the possibility of nephrolithiasis.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including microscopic hematuria and slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis, could be consistent with pyelonephritis.
The presence of a ureteral mass and partial obstruction, along with the patient's symptoms, could be consistent with ureteritis.
The ureteral mass and partial obstruction could be consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp.
The presence of a ureteral mass and partial obstruction, along with the patient's symptoms, could be consistent with malakoplakia.
The negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy results for malignancy, combined with the presence of a pedunculated ureteral tumor, are consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp.

rationales.F01: Gross hematuria is a common symptom of ureteral polyp and carcinoma.
rationales.F02: Intermittent right pelvic pain may be associated with ureteral stricture or nephrolithiasis.
rationales.F05: Treated pulmonary tuberculosis may increase the risk of malakoplakia.
rationales.F06: A 60-pack-year smoking history increases the risk of ureteral carcinoma.
rationales.F07: Microscopic hematuria is a common finding in ureteral polyp and carcinoma.
rationales.F09: Intravenous urography demonstrating a tubular filling defect is highly suggestive of ureteral polyp or carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Retrograde ureteropyelography confirming a tubular mass is highly suggestive of ureteral polyp or carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy results make ureteral carcinoma less likely.
rationales.F12: The absence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy on CT scan makes ureteral carcinoma less likely.
